skills.name: French West Africa: reform, Community and Guinea’s choice

note.text: French West African decolonisation developed through postwar reform and African political pressure. The Brazzaville Conference in 1944 considered reforms within empire, not immediate independence. The French Union of 1946 changed the framework but preserved colonial inequalities. The loi-cadre of 1956 expanded territorial political responsibility. In the 1958 referendum, Guinea rejected the proposed French Community and declared independence in October under Sékou Touré. Other territories followed different routes, with many attaining independence in 1960. Reform and independence are distinct stages.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to order constitutional changes and explain Guinea’s distinctive referendum choice. Builds on: different British transitions and postwar nationalism. Leads to: the Congo and Portuguese comparisons.

sections.heading: Explain the history

sections.heading: Follow the evidence and examples
sections.text: Sékou Touré and the Guinean Democratic Party favoured the No vote in {1958}. Guinea’s independence was proclaimed on {2} October. The break brought political and economic difficulties in relations with France, not an automatic end to every form of dependency. Contemporary official accounts must be compared with African perspectives; their language about reform can reflect the former colonial state’s viewpoint.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify actor, action, place and period before explaining a relationship. Use the practice text only for the claim it supports. Distinguish a cause, an event and an outcome; compare authentic sources before treating an interpretation as established. A sequence alone does not prove that every later outcome was inevitable.

cards.idea: Check a claim against the sequence, setting and limits of the evidence.
example: Brazzaville made every West African territory independent in {1944}. Correction: The conference’s reform framework remained imperial.
The French Union was identical to independent nationhood for every territory. Correction: Formal reform did not remove every inequality or reserved power.
The loi-cadre was adopted only after all territories were independent. Correction: The reform preceded the principal independence transitions.
Guinea followed the same Yes vote as every other territory. Correction: Its referendum choice was distinctive.
